chunks: Our father narrated, may God be pleased with him, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Fadal, from Abu Jamilah, from Rafaa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Night of Power is the beginning of the year and it is its end. Our elders, may God be pleased with them, agreed that it is the night of the twenty-third of the month of Ramadan, and the ritual bath (Ghusl) on that night is performed from the beginning of the night, and it is sufficient until its end.

key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Power/Decree, a significant night in Ramadan

ai.seo_question: When is Laylat al-Qadr and what is the ruling for Ghusl on that night?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records the consensus (Ijma') of the Shia scholars that Laylat al-Qadr is the 23rd of Ramadan, resolving the ambiguity of the 'beginning and end of the year' phrase by linking it to the spiritual renewal of the lunar cycle. The hadith further codifies the permissibility of performing Ghusl for this night at any point from Maghrib until Fajr, emphasizing the flexibility in ritual purification for this highly virtuous occasion.
